1. Draw BC = 6.5 cm.
2. At B, draw ∠CBE = 30°.
3. Cut BD = \(\frac{a}{2}\) = 2 cm on BE.
4. Join C, D.
5. Draw perpendicular bisector of CD to find midpoint.
6. At midpoint, draw angle equal to ∠BDC on opposite side, marking point A on BE.
\(\triangle ABC\) is required.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827904_jsb6a.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827904_jsb6a.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Draw two tangents from an external point to a circle with diameter a such that the angle between them is 2∠x.","marks":4,"answer":"Circle diameter = 4 cm, radius = 2 cm.
Angle between tangents = 2∠x = 2(30°) = 60°.
Steps:
1. Draw circle with center O, radius 2 cm.
2. Draw ∠AOB = 120° at center O (since 180° - 60° = 120°).
3. At points A and B on circle, draw perpendiculars to OA and OB respectively.
4. These perpendiculars meet at external point C.
5. AC and BC are tangents with included angle 60°.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827906_ui93.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827906_ui93.jpeg"}]

1. Draw BC = p = 4 cm.
2. At B, draw ∠CBF = ∠x = 45°.
3. Cut BD = q – p = 2 cm on BF.

6. CA meets BF at A.

5. Join A, B, C, D.

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Find the centre of any arc DEF.","marks":2,"answer":"To find centre of arc DEF:
- Take three points D, E, F on arc.
- Draw perpendicular bisectors of DE and EF.
- Their intersection is centre O.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_1x0io.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_1x0io.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, AP = AQ.","marks":4,"answer":"Join CP, CQ, CA.
- CP ⊥ AP, CQ ⊥ AQ (tangent ⊥ radius).
- In right triangles \(\triangle APC\) and \(\triangle AQC\):
Hypotenuse AC common, CP = CQ (radii).
So, \(\triangle APC \cong \triangle AQC\) (hypotenuse-side).
Hence, AP = AQ. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_qx90nr.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_qx90nr.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Draw a circumcircle of an equilateral triangle whose length of side is a.","marks":4,"answer":"Steps:

3. With centre O, radius OA, draw circumcircle.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_efkvur.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_efkvur.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"If DEF is an arc, then find its centre.","marks":2,"answer":"To find centre of arc DEF:

- Intersection is centre O.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_0iafwm.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_0iafwm.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"If two circles of centre M and N touch each other externally at the point P, then prove that the points M, P and N are collinear.","marks":4,"answer":"Since circles touch externally at P, they have common tangent at P.
- Draw tangent APB.
- MP ⊥ AP, NP ⊥ AP (radius ⊥ tangent).
- So, ∠MPN = ∠MPA + ∠APN = 90° + 90° = 180°.
- Hence, M, P, N are collinear. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_t8sl0g.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_t8sl0g.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Draw a circumcircle of the triangle whose sides are a, b and c.","marks":4,"answer":"Steps:

2. With B (radius c = 5.5 cm) and C (radius b = 4.5 cm), draw arcs meeting at A.
3. Join AB, AC.
4. Draw perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC meeting at O.
5. With centre O, radius OA, draw circumcircle.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_elnrup.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827907_elnrup.jpeg"}]

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"If F is an external point whose distance is 7 cm from the centre of a circle with diameter BC, then draw two tangents from the point F.","marks":4,"answer":"Circle diameter BC = 5 cm ⇒ radius = 2.5 cm, centre O.

2. Mark point F such that OF = 7 cm.

","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Draw a circle inscribed in the triangle BCD.","marks":4,"answer":"Steps for incircle of right-angled \(\triangle BCD\):
Since ∠BCD = 45° and triangle is right-angled, ∠D = 90° (the right angle must be at D since BC and CD form 45° angle at C).
1. Draw BC = 5 cm.
2. At C, draw ∠BCD = 45°.
3. At B, draw ∠DBC such that ray BD is perpendicular to BC, i.e., ∠DBC = 90°.
4. BD and CD meet at D, forming right angle at D.
5. Draw angle bisectors of any two angles (e.g., ∠B and ∠C) meeting at I.
